---
title: "Calculate traits from images"
author: "Patrick Pata"
date: "2025-11-26"
output: html_document
---

This script is for calculating trait values from the copepod images.

General procedure:
1. Calculate carbon content from segmented images
2. Apply random forest model to estimate carbon content for non-segmented images
3. Organize the trait values
4. Calculate the diapause respiration rate and duration relative to the in situ temperature of where the image was captured
5. Export data
6. Plot the results with the LOKI sizes and literature values (Figure S2)

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# 0. Load libraries and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(ggtext)
library(randomForest)

# The segmented images and morphological traits of calanoids
load("data/uvp6_CNN_segmentations_morphotraits_20260320.RData")

theme_set(theme_bw() +
            theme(text = element_text(size=14)))
source("functions/lipid_pump_toolkit.R")
```


#  1. Convert pixels to traits for segmented images
## Derive volume, dry weight, and carbon
```{r}
uvpRes <- 0.073
# Conversion factor to get total lipid mg C from total lipid mg used in Schmidt et al. 2018 based on the most common 36-carbon and 38-carbon chain lengths of NOW waxesters for C. glacialis and C. hyperboreus in (Kattner & Graeve 1991) 
lambda <- 0.81

# Conversion factor from volume (mm3) -> wet weight -> carbon weight
# For density assumed as 1, the value below is the Carbon % Wet weight for all calanoid copepod species
prosomeWW2C <- 0.09

# *** For the CNN segmented images ***
segmented.images <- segmented.images %>% 
  
# Calculate traits from pixels
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_length_mm = prosome_major * uvpRes) %>% 
  # Calculate minor axis based on prosome/lipid area and major axis (in pixels)
  mutate(minor_derived = (prosome_pixels / (pi * prosome_major/2)) * 2) %>% 
    # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * 
           (prosome_major/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid sac volume based on Tarling et al. (2022) eq1 derived from Miller et al. (1998) note that this is  based on cyclindrical volume approximation. According to Miller et al. (1998) the oblate spheroid volume approximation is less accurate.
  mutate(lipid_volume_mm3 = 
           (pi * lipid_area_mm2 ^ 2)/(4 * lipid_major * uvpRes)) %>% 
  
  # (Calculate lipid carbon based on area following Vogedes et al. 2010 with coefficients for 3 Arctic Calanus species
  mutate(totallipid_mass_mg = 0.197 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.38)) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mg = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.42)) %>%  
  
  # Calculate lipid carbon mass
  mutate(lipid_mass_mgC = totallipid_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC = waxester_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  
   # Calculate the carbon content of the prosome excluding the lipid sac
  mutate(structural_carbon_mgC = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 
           prosomeWW2C) %>% 
  
  mutate(prosome_total_mgC = structural_carbon_mgC + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
  
  # Calculate WE % TL (note both based on empirical models)
  mutate(we_perc_tl = (waxester_mass_mgC / lipid_mass_mgC) * 100) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid fullness as % carbon in lipid sac WE
  mutate(lipid_fullness = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_total_mgC * 100)
```

# 2. Alternative predictions for unsegmented images
## Train the Random Forest model
```{r, eval = FALSE}
df_for_rf <- segmented.images %>% 
  filter(source == "manual_segmentation") %>%
  select(c(object_id, structural_carbon_mgC, 
           waxester_mass_mgC, prosome_length_mm)) %>% 
  # Add predictors
  left_join(all.copepods.uvp6 %>% 
              select(object_id, Major:PerimMajor),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  select(-object_id)

# Random forest regression on prosome length
set.seed(888)
rf.model.prosome.mm <- randomForest(prosome_length_mm ~ .,
                      data = df_for_rf %>% 
                        select(-c(structural_carbon_mgC, waxester_mass_mgC)), 
                      importance = TRUE, proximity = TRUE)

# Random forest regression on structural carbon mass
set.seed(888)
rf.model.structural.mgC <- randomForest(structural_carbon_mgC ~ .,
                      data = df_for_rf %>% 
                        select(-c(waxester_mass_mgC, prosome_length_mm)), 
                      importance = TRUE, proximity = TRUE)

# Random forest regression on lipid (wax ester) mass
set.seed(888)
rf.model.lipid.mgC <- randomForest(waxester_mass_mgC ~ .,
                      data = df_for_rf %>% 
                        select(-c(structural_carbon_mgC, prosome_length_mm)), 
                      importance = TRUE, proximity = TRUE)
rf.model.structural.mgC 
rf.model.prosome.mm
rf.model.lipid.mgC 

# # Export the RF models
# save(rf.model.structural.mgC, rf.model.prosome.mm, rf.model.lipid.mgC,
#      file = "functions/random_forest_carbon_trait_models_20260321.RData")
```

## Predict traits with RF
```{r}
# Open the model generated in the chunk above
load("functions/random_forest_carbon_trait_models_20260321.RData")

other.calanoid.images <- all.copepods.uvp6 %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% segmented.images$object_id) %>% 
  filter(object_annotation_status == "validated") %>% 
  filter(traits_from_RF == T)

# Apply the Random forest models which directly predict for structural and lipidWE carbon in mgC
structural_predicted <-  predict(rf.model.structural.mgC,
               newdata = other.calanoid.images %>% 
                 select(Major:PerimMajor), predict.all = T)

lipid_predicted <- predict(rf.model.lipid.mgC,
               newdata = other.calanoid.images %>% 
                 select(Major:PerimMajor), predict.all = T)

prosome_length_predicted <- predict(rf.model.prosome.mm,
               newdata = other.calanoid.images %>% 
                 select(Major:PerimMajor), predict.all = T)

other.calanoid.images$structural_carbon_mgC <- structural_predicted$aggregate
other.calanoid.images$waxester_mass_mgC <- lipid_predicted$aggregate
other.calanoid.images$prosome_length_mm <- prosome_length_predicted$aggregate

# Calculate total carbon and lipid fullness
other.calanoid.images <- other.calanoid.images %>% 
  mutate(prosome_total_mgC = structural_carbon_mgC + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
  mutate(lipid_fullness = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_total_mgC * 100) %>% 
  mutate(source = if_else(object_annotation_category == "Calanoida",
                          "RF Calanoida", NA),
         source = if_else(object_annotation_category == "Copepoda<Maxillopoda",
                          "RF Copepoda", source),
         source = if_else(object_annotation_category %in% 
                            c("Calanus","top-bottom<with visible lipid sac",
                              "side<with visible lipid sac"),
                          "Random Forest", source))
```


# 3. Organize data indiv_traits dataframe
This includes all images of Calanus and large copepods. Images from profiles not included in the analysis are also included but will be excluded later in the analysis.
```{r}
indiv_traits <- segmented.images %>% 
  select(object_id, object_annotation_category, source,
         Site = sample_stationid, Cruise = sample_cruise,
         sample_id, object_depth_max,
         prosome_length_mm,
         prosome_total_mgC, structural_carbon_mgC,
         waxester_mass_mgC, lipid_fullness, 
         temperature_kelvin) %>% 
  bind_rows(other.calanoid.images %>% 
              select(object_id, object_annotation_category, source,
                     Site = sample_stationid, Cruise = sample_cruise,
                     sample_id, object_depth_max,
                     prosome_length_mm,
                     prosome_total_mgC, structural_carbon_mgC,
                     waxester_mass_mgC, lipid_fullness,
                     temperature_kelvin)) %>% 
  
  # Clarify sources
  # Assign source details, for non-"Calanus" category, identify taxa category
  mutate(source = if_else(source == "CNN_segmentation", 
                          "CNN segmentation", source),
         source = if_else(source == "manual_segmentation",
                          "Manual segmentation", source)) %>% 
  mutate(source = factor(source,
                          levels = c("Random Forest",
                                     "CNN segmentation", "Manual segmentation",
                                     "RF Calanoida", "RF Copepoda"))) %>%
  
  # Assign taxa names based on validated categorization
  mutate(taxa = if_else(object_annotation_category %notin% 
                          c("Calanoida", "Copepoda<Maxillopoda"),
                        "Calanus","Copepoda")) %>% 
  mutate(taxa = if_else(object_annotation_category == "Calanoida",
                        "Calanoida", taxa)) %>% 
  mutate(taxa = factor(taxa, levels = c("Copepoda","Calanoida","Calanus"))) %>% 
  select(-object_annotation_category)

```


# 4. Calculate diapause respiration rate, potential diapause duration, and total C respired
In Maps et al. (2014) the values for b are 2.27 +- 0.37 10-7 and activation energy 0.6 +- 0.092.
Use lower range of b = 2.27-0.37 and eV = 0.6-0.092, upper range of b = 2.27+0.37 eV = 0.6+0.092.
Note that in Visser et al. (2017) and Tarling et al. (2022), b is rounded to 2.3*10^-7.
```{r}
# Coefficients of the dormant/diapause respiration equation (Maps et al. 2014):
bb <- 2.27# Metabolic constant (x 10-7)
eV <- 0.6 # Activation energy
bb_se <- 0.37 # Standard error of the metabolic constant
eV_se <- 0.092 # Standard error of the activation energy
# Adjust respiration rate based on temperature

indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  # Calculate diapause respiration rate and duration
  mutate(mass_ugC = structural_carbon_mgC * 1000,
         WE_ugC = waxester_mass_mgC * 1000) %>% 
  mutate(respirationRate_ugCday = 
           (bb*10^-7 ) * (mass_ugC^0.75) * 
           exp(eV * (temperature_kelvin-273)/ 
                 ((8.62*10^-5)*temperature_kelvin*273)) * 86400) %>% 
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day = 
           (0.8*WE_ugC)/(respirationRate_ugCday)) %>% 

  # Cap the diapause duration capped to 240 days
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_cap = if_else(diapauseDuration_day > 240,
                                                240, diapauseDuration_day)) %>% 
  # The total C respired for the entire duration of diapause by the individual (ug C)
  mutate(diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC = 
           respirationRate_ugCday * diapauseDuration_day_cap) %>%  
  select(-c(mass_ugC, WE_ugC, diapauseDuration_day_cap)) 

# Add the minimum and maximum respiration based on standard error
indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  mutate(mass_ugC = structural_carbon_mgC * 1000,
         WE_ugC = waxester_mass_mgC * 1000) %>% 
  # Indv respiration rate
  mutate(respirationRate_ugCday_min  =
           ((bb - bb_se)*10^-7 ) * (mass_ugC^0.75) * 
           exp((eV - eV_se) * (temperature_kelvin-273)/ 
                 ((8.62*10^-5)*temperature_kelvin*273)) * 86400) %>% 
  mutate(respirationRate_ugCday_max  =
           ((bb + bb_se)*10^-7 ) * (mass_ugC^0.75) * 
           exp((eV + eV_se) * (temperature_kelvin-273)/ 
                 ((8.62*10^-5)*temperature_kelvin*273)) * 86400) %>% 
  # Diapause duration
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_min = 
           (0.8*WE_ugC)/(respirationRate_ugCday_min)) %>% 
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_max = 
           (0.8*WE_ugC)/(respirationRate_ugCday_max)) %>% 
  # Cap the diapause duration capped to 240 days
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_cap_min = if_else(diapauseDuration_day_min > 240,
                                                240, diapauseDuration_day_min)) %>% 
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_cap_max = if_else(diapauseDuration_day_max > 240,
                                                240, diapauseDuration_day_max)) %>% 
  # The total C respired for the entire duration of diapause by the individual (ug C)
  mutate(diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC_min = 
           respirationRate_ugCday_min * diapauseDuration_day_cap_min) %>%  
  mutate(diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC_max = 
           respirationRate_ugCday_max * diapauseDuration_day_cap_max) %>%  
  select(-c(diapauseDuration_day_cap_min, diapauseDuration_day_cap_max))
```



# 5. Export trait data
The indiv_traits dataframe includes images of individuals classified as "Calanus spp" and were segmented manually or with CNN (or the RF predictions when the CNN was bad). It also includes the RF predicted structural and lipid carbon values for images with major axis length >3 mm and were validated and classified as Calanoida/Copepoda, which are likely to be Calanus spp.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
save(indiv_traits, 
     volumes.df, region_rename, Amund_UVP6_meta,
     file = "data/uvp6_images_calculated_traits_20260321.RData")
```
